title: Pixar Films
description: Release years, directors, plots across the Pixar canon.

questions.prompt: What year was Toy Story released?
questions.explanation: Toy Story premiered in November 1995 as the world's first feature-length fully computer-animated film, directed by John Lasseter.

questions.prompt: What year was Up released?
questions.explanation: Up (2009) was the first animated film and first 3D film ever to open the Cannes Film Festival, and the second animated Best Picture nominee.

questions.prompt: Who directed Up, Inside Out, and Soul?
questions.explanation: Pete Docter is Pixar's Chief Creative Officer since 2018, succeeding John Lasseter; he's won three Best Animated Feature Oscars.

questions.prompt: Who directed The Incredibles and Ratatouille?
questions.explanation: Brad Bird joined Pixar after directing The Iron Giant (1999); he also directed Incredibles 2 (2018) and live-action film Tomorrowland.

questions.prompt: In which country is Coco set?
questions.explanation: Coco (2017) is set in the fictional Mexican town of Santa Cecilia; the film was named after Miguel's great-grandmother.

questions.prompt: What instrument does Joe Gardner play in Soul?
questions.explanation: Jazz pianist Jon Batiste performed Joe's piano parts; the film's original score was composed by Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross of Nine Inch Nails.

questions.prompt: What mythical creatures are the Lightfoot brothers in Onward?
questions.explanation: Onward (2020) is set in a suburban fantasy world where magic has been replaced by technology; brothers Ian and Barley are voiced by Tom Holland and Chris Pratt.

questions.prompt: What year was Finding Nemo released?
questions.explanation: Finding Nemo (2003) was directed by Andrew Stanton and won the Best Animated Feature Oscar; it held the record for highest-grossing animated film for years.

questions.prompt: What year was Ratatouille released?
questions.explanation: Ratatouille (2007) won Best Animated Feature; Brad Bird took over directing duties from Jan Pinkava just 18 months before release and reworked the story.

questions.prompt: What year was WALL-E released?
questions.explanation: WALL-E (2008) was directed by Andrew Stanton; its first 40 minutes are nearly dialogue-free, an artistic risk that paid off with Oscar wins.

questions.prompt: In Luca, what kind of creatures are Luca and Alberto?
questions.explanation: Luca and Alberto transform into human form when dry; the film draws visual inspiration from Hayao Miyazaki's Ponyo and Studio Ghibli.

questions.prompt: In which Italian region is Luca set?
questions.explanation: The fictional town of Portorosso was based on real Cinque Terre villages like Vernazza and Manarola in the Liguria region.

questions.prompt: In Turning Red, what animal does Mei transform into?
questions.explanation: Director Domee Shi based the story on her own teenage years; Turning Red was Pixar's first feature directed solely by a woman.

questions.prompt: In which Canadian city is Turning Red set?
questions.explanation: Turning Red (2022) is set in Toronto in 2002, with details like the CN Tower, SkyDome, and TTC streetcars based on director Domee Shi's hometown.

questions.prompt: Which Pixar film won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature in 2018?
questions.explanation: Coco won at the 2018 ceremony for the 2017 film; it also won Best Original Song for 'Remember Me' by Kristen Anderson-Lopez and Robert Lopez.

questions.prompt: Who directed Coco?
questions.explanation: Lee Unkrich also directed Toy Story 3 (2010); Adrian Molina served as co-director on Coco and is now directing Coco 2.

questions.prompt: What year was Brave released?
questions.explanation: Brave (2012) was Pixar's first film with a female protagonist and first directed by a woman (Brenda Chapman, before she was replaced by Mark Andrews).

questions.prompt: What is the name of the princess in Brave?
questions.explanation: Merida was officially inducted as the 11th Disney Princess in 2013; she's the only one created by Pixar rather than Walt Disney Animation.

questions.prompt: In Elemental, what are the two main characters made of?
questions.explanation: Ember (fire) and Wade (water) live in Element City; the film is an immigration metaphor inspired by director Peter Sohn's Korean-American upbringing.

questions.prompt: What year was Cars released?
questions.explanation: Cars (2006) was the final Pixar film produced before Disney acquired the studio in 2006 for $7.4 billion.

questions.prompt: Who directed the original Cars?
questions.explanation: John Lasseter, Pixar's co-founder, also directed Toy Story 1 and 2, A Bug's Life, and Cars 2; he left the company in 2018.

questions.prompt: What year was Monsters, Inc. released?
questions.explanation: Monsters, Inc. (2001) was Pete Docter's directorial debut and Pixar's fourth feature film; it earned over $577 million worldwide.

questions.prompt: Which Pixar film is a prequel set in Monstropolis university?
questions.explanation: Monsters University (2013) shows how Mike and Sulley first met as rivals in college; it's Pixar's only prequel feature to date.

questions.prompt: In Lightyear, who voices Buzz Lightyear?
questions.explanation: Lightyear (2022) is presented as the in-universe movie that inspired Andy's Buzz toy; Chris Evans replaced Tim Allen for the human Buzz role.

questions.prompt: In Toy Story 3, who does Andy give his toys to at the end?
questions.explanation: Toy Story 3 (2010) was the first animated film to gross over $1 billion; the toy-handoff finale made it the rare sequel to win Best Animated Feature.
